method.label: List and check the possible divisors

annotationRationale: The gcd and lcm conditions restrict n to multiples of 15 that divide 180. Listing factors makes the candidate check exhaustive.
sourceMethod: Follows the first official method, which enumerates and checks six candidates. Adds n=15k with k dividing 12 to justify completeness.

review.mathCheck: The conditions force \(15\mid n\mid180\). Writing \(n=15k\) gives exactly the six divisors of 12 as possible k values. All table entries check correctly; only \(n=60\) works, giving digit sum 6, choice B.
review.sourceMethodCheck: The mapped source is MAA 2022 AMC 10A Problem 7 on attached page 5. The candidate faithfully adapts its first, tabular method and independently explains why the candidate list is exhaustive.
review.annotationCheck: The assessed GCF/LCM and supporting divisor-listing roles match the work. The argument is reconstructible at AMC 12 level, with no omitted cases or key conflict.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The exact GCF, LCM, and factors-and-multiples links fit the checks and enumeration of the factors of 12.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: 4.OA.B.4 supports listing factors of 12, without demonstrating prime/composite classification. The partial 6.NS.B.4 links support GCF checks with inputs at most 100; the 180 row exceeds that bound, and every LCM check exceeds its input bound of 12. Distributive rewriting is absent.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: cnm_p158 and cnm_p159 are correctly assessed; cnm_p153 supports the exhaustive restriction and list. Prime factorization is unnecessary for this chosen method.
